title: Times Tables: 2s, 5s and 10s (KS1)
subject: Maths
strapline: The first three tables — and the patterns that make them stick.
facts: Multiplying means counting in equal groups: 3×5 means three groups of five.
The 2 times table is doubling: 2×6 is double 6, which is 12.
The 10 times table always ends in 0: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50...
The 5 times table always ends in 5 or 0: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25...
Multiplication can be done in any order: 2×5 = 5×2 = 10.
You can show a fact as an array — rows and columns of dots: 2 rows of 5 = 10.
Skip counting out loud (2, 4, 6, 8...) helps you learn the pattern.

quick_quiz.q: Double 7 is the same as 2 × 7. What is it?

teacher_tips: Link 2s to doubles and 10s to place value the children already know.
Chant while clapping or stepping — movement helps the pattern stick.
Show the array both ways round to prove 2×5 and 5×2 are equal.
